standard_prerequisites: cohomology and base change for proper flat finite presentation morphisms giving a perfect E = Rf_*O_X whose formation commutes with base change
the jump-locus lemma: where H^0 of a perfect complex is locally free of rank 1 the locus is universal closed and the map factors
the diagonal section argument splitting a direct image with a section
the cut-complex lemma splitting a perfect complex where H^0 fibre-surjects
the ring fact that an algebra invertible as a module over the base is the base
core_obligations: Prove: (a) f_*O_X = O_Y and this survives any base change; (b) etale locally on Y the decomposition Rf_*O_X = O_Y plus a summand P perfect of tor amplitude in [1, infinity)
proof_roadmap: Work etale locally, Y affine; E = Rf_*O_X is perfect with base-change compatible formation, so the degree-zero fibre cohomology equals kappa(y), giving beta_0 <= 1 everywhere
The jump-locus lemma yields a universal closed subscheme j : Z to Y where H^0(Lj^*E) is invertible

Base-change compatibility identifies Lf^*E with Rpr_{1,*}O_{X x_Y X}; the diagonal section splits Rpr_{1,*} as O_X plus a summand, so O_X is a direct summand of H^0(Lf^*E) and f factors through Z; since X to Y is an fppf cover, Z = Y
Hence f_*O_X is invertible as a module, and the unit map O_Y to f_*O_X is an isomorphism by the invertible-algebra fact; assumptions pass to base changes so (a) holds generally
For (b): the fibre-surjectivity of O_Y to H^0(E tensor kappa(y)) lets the cut-complex lemma split Rf_*O_X = O_Y plus a perfect summand P of tor amplitude [1, infinity) near each y
difficulty_reason: H2: base change plus a jump-locus argument and a splitting argument; every step is written out with its quoted lemma.
